environment.description: NestJS microservice deployed in a hardened Kubernetes pod on EKS with the following runtime confinement: (1) Pod runs with a custom seccomp profile (runtime/default augmented with blocked connect() to link-local range via BPF filter attached at cgroup level using Cilium L3/L4 NetworkPolicy denying egress to 169.254.0.0/16), (2) Container filesystem uses pivot_root into /app with a read-only overlayfs where the upper layer is a tmpfs mounted at /app/tmp — effectively a chroot jail where /proc, /sys, and /etc are bind-mounted as empty read-only directories, meaning /etc/resolv.conf is a static file pointing to CoreDNS and credential files like /root/.aws or environment variables from IMDS are inaccessible, (3) IMDSv2 enforced with hop limit of 1 on the underlying node (HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1) which combined with the pod network namespace means metadata token PUT requests from within the pod receive no response due to TTL expiration at the veth boundary.

config.network_policy: Cilium L3/L4 policy denying egress to 169.254.0.0/16 CIDR
config.filesystem: pivot_root /app, overlayfs read-only, /proc /sys /etc empty bind mounts
config.sensitive_files: none present in chroot - /app contains only application code and node_modules
config.dns: CoreDNS with no rebinding protection but egress blocked at L3
